worksheet.title: Same and Different
worksheet.subtitle: Matching what is the same
worksheet.learning_goal: I can find the card that is the same, and the one that is different.

parts.title: Bit looks for a match
parts.text: Bit holds up a card. Help Bit find the card that is the SAME. Cards that look alike are a MATCH.

parts.title: Which one is the same as ●?
parts.note: The circle ● is the same as Bit's card. Circle the match.

parts.title: Find the same as  ★
parts.prompt: Circle the card that is the same as the star.   ●   ★   ▲

parts.title: Find the same as  ■
parts.prompt: Circle the card that is the same as the square.   ●   ▲   ■

parts.title: You try — which is different?
parts.prompt: Three are the same and one is different. Circle the one that is DIFFERENT.   ●   ●   ▲   ●

parts.title: Big idea
parts.text: Matching means finding what is the same. Computers match too — like finding the same face in your photos!

parts.title: Goal
parts.text: Children match a target to the card that is the SAME, then spot the one that is DIFFERENT. Comparing by attribute (same/different) is a core computational-thinking skill — recognizing equality is how computers find and group matching things.

parts.title: Kindergarten frame (Ontario)
text: Problem Solving and Innovating — children compare and match objects by attribute as they make sense of their world.
No reading required of the child: read each prompt aloud; the child responds by circling.

parts.title: Materials
parts.text: The printed worksheet + a pencil/crayon. Optional: pairs of matching cards or objects to match by hand first.

parts.title: Run it (about 15 min)
text: 1. MODEL: hold up a circle. 'Find the one that is the same.' Point to the ● — that is the match.
2. GUIDED: do Exercise 1 together — the star matches the star.
3. YOU TRY: children do Exercise 2, then Exercise 3 (the odd one out) on their own.
4. Connect: 'Computers match too — that is how a phone finds the same face in your photos.'

parts.title: Answer key (modelled by the run-gate)
text: Ex 1 — circle the ★ (the star). Ex 2 — circle the ■ (the square).
Ex 3 — circle the ▲; it is different because the other three are all circles.

parts.title: Watch for & differentiate
text: Common slip: circling more than one — remind them there is exactly one match.
Simplify: match real identical objects by hand before using the page.
Extend: ask 'how is it different?' (shape, corners) to build describing language.
Movement option: hold up a card and have children point to or run to the matching card on the wall.

parts.title: Success looks like
parts.text: The child circles the one matching card for the targets, and identifies the single different card in Exercise 3.
